contextual.summary: Bristol makes contextual offers of up to two grades below the standard entry requirements to eligible home applicants who attended an aspiring state school or college, live in an IMD quintile 1 or 2 area, completed a Bristol widening participation programme, spent three months or more in care, or were eligible for free school meals.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades below the standard entry requirements

criteria.detail: Attended an 'aspiring' state school or college, meaning one with low average attainment and low progression to higher education, as shown on Bristol's published lists of aspiring schools and colleges for the 2027 cycle (England and Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland, Isle of Man)
Live in a home postcode in an IMD quintile 1 or 2 area (the 40% most deprived neighbourhoods), based on the home address on your UCAS form

Completed a University of Bristol widening participation programme: Access to Bristol, Discover Bristol, Insight into Bristol summer school, Next Step Bristol or Virtual Summer School (Bristol Scholars get a tailored offer rather than a contextual one)
Spent three months or more in local authority care
Been eligible for free school meals during your secondary education

contextual.rulesText: Contextual offers are only made to applicants with home fee status who are studying A-levels and/or the International Baccalaureate and apply through UCAS (not for CertHE Foundation or Gateway courses). You may be eligible if one of the listed statements applies to you; eligibility is worked out from your UCAS application and you are automatically considered.

source.evidence: Our contextual offer is a grade reduction of up to two grades below the standard entry requirements.

programmes.name: Access to Bristol
programmes.summary: A scheme for local state-educated students to experience Bristol through study-skills, subject sessions and on-campus afternoons; completers are guaranteed a contextual offer or interview.
programmes.whoCanApply: Home-fee students at a state school or college who live in a BA, BS or other local postcode within an hour's journey of Bristol (including south Wales) and are in the first or second year of A-level study (or equivalent).
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Open only to students who meet all of: home fee student; currently attend a state school or college; live in a BA, BS or other local postcode within an hour's journey of the University (including south Wales); in the first or second year of A-level study (or equivalent); have the academic ability to study at Bristol (meeting the GCSE entry requirements for the subject stream and studying any required Level 3 subjects). If a stream is oversubscribed, priority goes to students who are or have been eligible for free school meals, live in an IMD quintile 1 or 2 area, are mature students, are Black, Asian or of mixed background featuring one of these groups, have spent three months or more in care, are estranged, are from Gypsy, Traveller, Roma, Showmen and Boater communities, attend an aspiring state school or college, are from another minority ethnic background, are the first in their family to go to university, have caring responsibilities, have refugee status, have a disability or have a parent or carer who serves or has served in the UK Armed Forces.
benefits: Guaranteed contextual offer (typically two A-level grades below standard entry requirements) for courses that don't routinely interview, if you successfully complete the scheme and meet the course requirements
Subject sessions with academics and current students, plus tailored information, advice and guidance on higher education
programmes.offerReduction: Typically two A-level grades below standard entry requirements
programmes.subjects: Subject streams; Economics runs as an autumn stream (Year 13 and Access to HE; Year 12 by invitation only), and Business management and Social sciences run as spring streams for Year 12

programmes.name: Discover Bristol
programmes.summary: A Year 13 programme of five online sessions (Bristol overview, UCAS and personal statement guidance, funding, study skills, careers) for state-school students from lower socio-economic groups; completers are guaranteed a contextual offer or interview.
programmes.whoCanApply: Home-fee students at a state school or college in their final year of A-level study who will apply to Bristol through UCAS and are eligible for free school meals or live in an IMD quintile 1 or 2 area.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must be a home fee student; currently attend a state school or college; be in the final year of A-level study (or equivalent); have the academic ability to study at Bristol (including GCSE entry requirements and required Level 3 subjects) and the potential to meet the contextual entry requirements; have applied or will apply to Bristol through UCAS by the deadline; and be eligible for free school meals OR live in an IMD quintile 1 or 2 postcode area. Open to students who have not already taken part in another Bristol widening participation programme (Access to Bristol, Bristol Scholars, Insight into Bristol, Next Step Bristol, Virtual Summer School). If oversubscribed, priority goes to applicants who meet further widening participation criteria (for example mature students, some ethnic groups, care experienced, estranged, first generation, caring responsibilities, refugees, disabled). No late applications are accepted.
benefits: Guaranteed contextual offer (typically two A-level grades below standard entry requirements) for courses that don't routinely interview, if you successfully complete the programme and meet the course requirements

notes: All course facts are for September 2027 entry. Bristol hasn't published 2028-entry course pages yet (checked 2026-10-20: the 2028 address of the BSc Economics course page returned 'Not Found'), so check again before applying.

The BSc courses recorded here need A-level Mathematics. BA Economics (L150) and Politics, Philosophy and Economics (VL20) don't need A-level Maths but ask for grade 7 in GCSE Mathematics (the advanced numeracy requirement).

Study-abroad versions (4 years, own UCAS codes): Economics L105 (L101 with a modern language), Economics and Finance LN15, Economics and Accounting LN16, Economics and Management LN17, Economics and Politics LL14. Economics and Accounting with Professional Placement can't be applied for directly; students transfer from LN14.
Home students on a full-year study or work placement pay 15% of the full tuition fee and those on a whole-year industrial placement pay 20% (2026/27 figures).

Not added, to keep to 8 courses: Economics and Econometrics BSc (L140, A*AA including Mathematics), Economics and Data Science BSc (L1G1, A*AA including Mathematics), Philosophy and Economics BSc (VL51, AAA including Mathematics) and MSci Economics with Innovation.

EPQ: accepted to meet standard literacy conditions but not in place of an A-level. Core Maths isn't accepted in place of A-level Mathematics. General Studies, Global Perspectives and Critical Thinking aren't accepted as A-levels, and there is no preference for four A-levels or AS-levels.

Guaranteed offers are a separate scheme from contextual offers: applicants with a BS, BA1, BA2, BA3, BA5, BA14 or BA15 home postcode at a state school, Access to HE applicants, completers of Bristol widening participation programmes and applicants eligible for free school meals may be considered for one (https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/entry-requirements-qualifications/guaranteed-offers/).
Bristol delivered its own Sutton Trust Summer School for the last time in 2024, so there's no current Sutton Trust offer at Bristol to record.

Bristol's own living-costs survey says undergraduates spent an average of £1,401 a month in 2025/26, including about £775.78 a month on rent or mortgage (https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/advice/set-up-finances/living-expenses/).

Bristol's 2027 admissions statements for the courses recorded here (PDFs linked from https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/apply/admissions-statements/: Economics, Accounting and Finance, and Politics) say applications are scored on GCSE results (20%) and A-level results (80%), the personal statement is not normally considered (it may be used to separate applicants with the same academic score), and applicants are not routinely interviewed.
